title: Time's up
body:
Well bummer. Great challenge and wish I would have had a better showing.

What is working:

- client start()
- server authentication
- The cgroup is almost getting setup. last was trying to figure out why the io.max setting wasn't working
- wrote something quickly to read the 

In place to some degree but not tested:
- the exec call to launch the process
- a way to clone the status from the job for the status call

Other things:

To manage the state of the jobs, I planned on storing the jobs in a map, using the id as a key.   And another map for username -> []jobid for authentication /job lookup type stuff.

The tokenringbuffer (using byte slices) I wrote implements an io.ReadCloser, io.Writer, and can also take itself as an argument.  Thereby being its own buffer between the Job buffer and clients.  Clients would actually be pulling data from a separate buffer that was buffering the Job output buffer, so only one reader and writer per job buffer.

Seems like the rest of what remained beyond that boils down to testing and some basic things left to finish.  I tried to tackle the harder stuff first and was ready to start testing/integrating that stuff the end of Friday.

Lessons Learned:

TLDR: Ubuntu userspace namespacing (and maybe AppArmor as well?  Not sure).   Ugh.

If I could do it again, I would have used a Linux machine for coding just to have a faster turn around time to work through all of the details of writing out the cgroups correct.  I did eventually just start coding on a Ubuntu VM once I was ready to start testing cgroup v2.

I have a M1 MacBook Pro and was testing with a Ubuntu 24 VM.  The biggest hurdles was not realizing that in the latest release, Ubuntu has added [namespacing for user processes via systemd](https://ubuntu.com/blog/whats-new-in-security-for-ubuntu-24-04-lts) and it totally tripped me up.  Given the M1, it really eliminates a lot of Linux VM options.  

Not having worked in userland in quite some time, I eventually thought the wonkiness that was happening was systemd related and didn't really see any other good options for testing on a VM as most everything uses systemd now.  I didn't realize it was specifcally a new Ubuntu thing for userland processes until today.  I also had to figure out that Ubuntu uses cgroup v1 by default and I had to reconfigure it for v2.  It's some sort of mixed mode by default where it looks like it's v2, but its not.

Finally figured out why nothing made sense even with running things as root.  Installed an older version of Ubuntu server and was finally able to start working through getting cgroup v2 working.  (After other attempts of trying to disable the namespacing, fire-up some other VMs, etc). I was last working on setting io.max.

I have definitely learned a lot, but bummed that it took me so long to figure out that namespacing for user proceses via systemd in Ubuntu was now a thing.  I have mostly been working with containers for the past 7 years or so; definitely rusty at userland stuff.  So I just haven't worked with systemd much.

I was "code complete" on Friday to start testing my cgroup code, but wasn't in a place where testing it made sense until early afteroon on Tuesday  Wasted way too much time on getting to a place of being able to test against.  Bummer, I'm pretty confident I could have finished had I not ran into several days of that mess.
